title: Gigaro, Cap Lardier and Cap Taillat from La Croix-Valmer
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: La Croix-Valmer takes on another scale as soon as you follow its shoreline. Gigaro, Cap Lardier and Cap Taillat reveal a commune widely open towards protected natural spaces.
content:
La Croix-Valmer keeps a discreet centre, yet its personality extends above all along the coast. As soon as one reaches Gigaro and then the headlands, the walk moves from a village interpretation to one of open space, protected vegetation and marine lines.

Gigaro as a landscape threshold

Gigaro is not only a well-known beach. It is also a threshold. From there, the commune shifts towards routes where shoreline, slopes and long views prevail over the built fabric.

Cap Lardier and Cap Taillat, a natural continuity

These headlands remind you that La Croix-Valmer belongs to a wider coastal whole than a single beachfront. They reveal protected environments, the weight of Mediterranean botany and a much broader scale of walking.

Why this commune remains distinctive

La Croix-Valmer does not seek the effect of a hill village. Its strength lies in this calm passage between village, vineyards, beaches and broad headlands. It is another way into the gulf, more lateral and more natural.
